question.leadin: This city was the projected destination of a 1965 protest march that began in Selma.
question.text: Name this Alabama capital, the site of a bus boycott that began in 1955.
question.clue: This city was the destination of a march, whose participants were attacked by police on "Bloody Sunday" while crossing the Edmund Pettus Bridge in Selma.

swap.leadin: Answer some questions about tragic events concerning a certain family.
swap.text: During the 1968 California primaries, Sirhan Sirhan shot and killed this brother of JFK in a hotel.
swap.clue: This man formed a team to investigate Jimmy Hoffa, the head of the Teamsters Union.

question.text: The Interstate Highway System was developed during the 1950s under this President, who was inspired by the Autobahn while Supreme Commander of Allied forces during World War II.
question.clue: One of this man's Cabinet members, Charles Wilson, said during confirmation hearings that "for years I thought what was good for the country was good for General Motors."

swap.leadin: Give the following about the presidential Election of 1948.
swap.text: In the election, racist Strom Thurmond ran with this third party, whose common nickname is a mashup of"Democrat" and a term for the South. This party's official name was a political concept commonly cited inarguments for nineteenth-century slavery and twentieth-century segregation.
swap.clue: Strom Thurmond won four states running on the platform of this party, nicknamed for its southern origin. This party supported a bunch of segregationist policies.

question.leadin: During this event, the Youth International Party attempted to nominate a pig named Pigasus for president.
question.text: Name this event, notable for its violent protests, which resulted in the nomination of Hubert Humphrey.
question.clue: The aftermath of this event led to the adoption of the McGovern-Fraser Commission and the "Rights in Conflict" study by Daniel Walker.

swap.leadin: Answer these questions about the writings and speeches of Martin Luther King, Jr.
swap.text: MLK gave this speech in front of the Lincoln Memorial during the March on Washington for Jobs and Freedom. This speech states "let freedom ring".
swap.clue: The beginning of this speech states that "Five score years ago, a great American, in whose symbolic shadow we stand, signed the Emancipation Proclamation."

question.leadin: Justice Byron White argued in his dissent of this case that since interrogation is not coercive, the Fifth Amendment does not protect against self incrimination in the case of police questioning.
question.text: Name this Supreme Court case that ruled that suspects have the right to an attorney after its subject was forced to submit a confession. This case inspired a namesake set of rights, including the right to remain silent.
question.clue: The defendant in this case was killed during a knife fight at the La Amapola bar.

swap.leadin: They were organized after a favorable decision in Boynton v. Virginia.
swap.text: Name this 1961 civil rights movement, which Governor Patterson reluctantly protected by sending the Alabama National Guard.
swap.clue: With the SNCC, the Congress of Racial Equality organized this specific event following the success of sit-ins in 1960.

question.text: After the management at Constitution Hall refused to allow her to sing, Eleanor Roosevelt and Secretary of the Interior Harold Ickes arranged a free concert at the Lincoln Memorial where an audience of 75,000 gathered.

swap.text: When later asked about his casting the deciding vote in this 1986 case, Lewis Powell said, "I think I probably made a mistake on that one." Much maligned by gay rights groups, the ruling is likely to be overturned by the Supreme Court in the upcoming decision of Lawrence & Garner v. Texas. For 15 points-name this controversial Supreme Court case that upheld a Georgia law prohibiting homosexual sodomy.
swap.clue: Harry Blackmun's dissenting opinion in this case criticized Warren Burger's concurring opinion that "Judeo-Christian moral and ethical standards" and "millenia of moral teaching" justified one of Georgia's laws.

question.leadin: Philip Vera Cruz led a strike of unionized farm workers against grape growers in a California town named for this family.
question.text: Identify this [emphasize] middle name of a president who received policy advice from Mary McLeod Bethune and the Black Cabinet alongside his wife.
question.answerHtml: Delano [accept Delano grape strike; prompt on FDR or Franklin Delano Roosevelt by asking “which name?”; reject “Roosevelt” or “Franklin Roosevelt”]
question.clue: This name. A 1960s grape boycott led by Cesar Chavez originated in a California town of this name.

swap.text: The claim was filed with this federal agency that handles workplace discrimination cases. Clarence Thomas headed this agency before joining the Supreme Court.
swap.clue: ADA violations can be investigated by this federal agency that enforces laws against workplace discrimination. Clarence Thomas was head of this agency for eight years.

question.leadin: Sixteen-year old Larry Kayne was shot for marching in support of this event.
question.text: Identify this 1968 event that began after the deaths of Echol Cole and Robert Walker. An activist delivered the "I've Been to the Mountaintop" speech in support of this event at Mason Temple one day before his assassination.
question.clue: This event during which a group of predominantly African American workers walked off the job, much to the chagrin of Mayor Henry Loeb, a "white unity" advocate.

swap.leadin: This speech criticized the March on Washington by saying "[they] made you think you were going somewhere and you end up going nowhere."
swap.text: Name this speech that warned of a racial "powder keg" more dangerous than Russian atomic bombs. This speech exhorted African Americans of all faiths to fight for civil rights with either of its two title means.
swap.clue: This 1964 speech by Malcolm X expressed distrust that advent of voting rights would be any different from "running from the wolf to the fox," and suggested the second titular subject may prove necessary should the first one fail.

question.leadin: A likely apocryphal anecdote claims that this activist threw a 'shot glass that was heard around the world'.
question.text: Name this activist, who co-founded the group Street Transvestite Activist Revolutionaries along with Sylvia Rivera.
question.clue: This woman's middle name stood for "pay it no mind" and she was a founder of an organization which organized a 1970 march, the first of its kind.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about contributions made by Asian-Americans to the LGBT rights movement.
swap.text: The Daughters of Bilitis grew out of a social club organized by the Filipina immigrant Rosalie Bamberger as an alternative to these locations. The Stonewall riots began in one of these locations operated by the Mafia.
swap.answerHtml: gay bars [accept lesbian bars; accept gay taverns or lesbian taverns; prompt on inns by asking “the Stonewall Inn was what type of location?”]
swap.clue: One of these places controlled by mobster "Fat Tony" Lauria technically operated as a membership organization to skirt laws making it illegal to serve its clientele.

question.leadin: Answer the following about some twentieth-century martyrs depicted over the Great West Door of Westminster Abbey.
question.text: This co-founder of the Southern Christian Leadership Conference and author of Why We Can't Wait was assassinated by James Earl Ray in Memphis on April 4th, 1968.
question.answerHtml: Dr. Martin Luther King, Jr. (prompt on “Martin Luther King” or “King”)

swap.leadin: The Percy Jones Army Hospital in Battle Creek, Michigan, became a federal building complex named for three future senators who met there during World War II, each while receiving treatment for their wounded right arms.
swap.text: This man, whose arm had been hit by shrapnel on Utah Beach, became known as the "Conscience of the Senate." He sponsored the Immigration Act of 1965 with Emmanuel Celler.
